outlook.statement: Newsprint is being imported at 5% duty at very low rates due to dumping by foreign manufacturers and this has depressed the demand and prices of newsprint manufactured by Indian Paper Mills, thereby also affecting the demand of writing and printing paper as newsprint capacities are being diverted to writing and printing paper manufacture.
The installed capacity for writing and printing paper has increased significantly in the last four years, thereby affecting the demand as well as prices of the paper manufactured by your company.
Measures are being taken to save costs and rationalize operations, they are likely to yield positive results.
The trend in consumption of papers and notebooks and eco friendly papers are increasing continuously. It will result in good demand for the industrial product.
Based on current estimates the company expects the carrying amounts of these assets to be realised as stated in the financial statements.

risks: Newsprint import dumping at 5% duty depressing demand and prices
Significant increase in installed capacity for writing and printing paper affecting demand and prices
Raw material procurement from unrecognized sector (95% of total) affecting continuous supply
Sub-par utilization of capacities may lead to inadequate leverage benefits
Fire accident at manufacturing unit on 09 March 2025 causing damage to spares and stores inventory
Insurance claim settlement uncertainty - initial claim of Rs. 90,00,000 settled at Rs. 32,41,965
Slight delays in depositing statutory dues in few cases
Credit risk from Cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables, and other financial assets
Liquidity risk managed through rolling cash flow forecasts and committed credit lines
Market risk - Interest rate risk on long-term borrowings at variable rates
Actuarial risks: interest rate risk, salary risk, longevity risk for defined benefit plans
